title: Developer Velocity Toolkit: SDKs, Quickstarts & Docs Initiative
creator: Liam Chen
description: Initiative to consolidate and accelerate developer onboarding and task completion by publishing a coherent Developer Velocity Toolkit: a set of opinionated SDKs (Python/Node/Go), trimmed quickstarts for top 3 use cases (text generation, embeddings, chat), and a focused docs site path that surfaces best-practice prompts, batching guidance, and cost/latency tuning recipes. Goal: reduce time-to-first-successful-query for new signups from current baseline by 40% and increase 14-day active retention of new accounts using SDKs/quickstarts by 20%.
goals: Ship v0.1 SDKs for Python and Node with example apps
Publish 3 curated quickstarts (Text gen demo, Embeddings search, Chat + tools) with step-by-step scripts
Create a Docs 'Getting Productive' path that highlights cost and latency tradeoffs and recommended runtime configs
Instrument success metrics (time-to-first-successful-query, 14-day retention, quickstart completion rate) and hook into analytics dashboards
success_metrics: Reduce time-to-first-successful-query by 40% for new signups using toolkit
Increase 14-day retention of users who try SDK/quickstart by 20%
Achieve >= 75% quickstart completion rate for users who start a quickstart within 7 days
Track token cost per successful quickstart and aim for median cost < $0.15
acceptance_criteria: Public SDK packages published to npm and PyPI with semantic versioning and CHANGELOG
Three quickstarts live in docs with one-click Cloud Console templates and runnable GitHub repos
Docs path created with clear section for runtime cost/latency knobs and two worked examples showing batching/KV cache gains
Monitoring dashboards instrumented and linked in the ticket; baseline and target values recorded
Post-release checklist completed: security review, license check, and legal signoff for third-party samples
tasks: PM: finalize scope and prioritize quickstart scenarios (PM-11723-1)
Eng: implement and test SDK auth + streaming API surface (ENG-2418)
Design: quickstart UX and templates for Console (DES-402)
Docs: author quickstarts + Getting Productive path and include runbook examples
Infra: add telemetry hooks and events for quickstart completion and TTFQ metric
QA: test end-to-end reproducibility on Hosted and Dedicated environments
Release: publish packages, update docs sitemap, announce in release notes
risks_and_tradeoffs: Scope creep if we try to support too many SDK languages before stabilizing core UX; starting with Python + Node reduces breadth risk
Including complex features (streaming + function calling) increases QA time; plan: ship basic streaming + disable experimental features by default
Bundling opinionated tuning recommendations may conflict with large enterprise customers; docs will include explicit caveats and alternate paths
Telemetry reliance on Console events requires coordination with infra; if delayed, initial metrics will be sampled and backfilled
stakeholders: Engineering: Maya Rao (runtime), Carlos Jimenez (sdk lead)

Include explicit section on cost controls and recommended model variants for low-cost evaluation workloads.
Plan a short 'launch week' with engineering on-call to handle integration issues from external users.
